jobs.goal: Produce a reviewable result for node verdict-confidence-split
jobs.title: Split verdict confidence into criteria-confidence and completeness so the score is trustable
jobs.why:
A practice run exposed a calibration bug that directly undermines the goal of
trusting the loop at face value. A node whose code fully satisfied every
criterion (semantic judgments all pass at 0.9-0.99 with line-level evidence)
received an overall confidence of 0.18. Two distortions caused this:

1. The blend uses min(deterministic_floor, semantic). When the deterministic
   floor is indeterminate-dominated — which is precisely WHY the semantic phase
   was invoked — that low, admittedly-uncertain floor overrides the semantic
   phase built to decide. The weakest signal wins, backwards.
2. Missing execution artifacts correctly gate the VERDICT to needs-more-evidence,
   but the single confidence scalar then conflates "unsure the code works"
   (false here) with "paperwork/trail missing" (true here).

Fix: report against the receipt contract instead of one blended scalar. The
criteria signal says how sure we are the code meets the spec; the completeness
signal says whether the required trail is present; the graph-readiness signal
says whether the human has enough evidence to advance graph truth. And when
the floor is indeterminate-dominated, defer to the semantic confidence rather
than min()-ing it away. This makes a built-but-untrailed node read as ~0.95
criteria-confidence with a needs-more-evidence verdict — honest, not 0.18.

Runtime commit 7f803ce added the field names, but it still populates
criteria_confidence as a compatibility alias of overall confidence and the
semantic blend still min()s against an indeterminate floor. This node remains
blocked on the receipt contract, then owns the real calibration change.

jobs.goal: Produce a reviewable result for node pi-evaluator-harness
jobs.title: Drive the semantic evaluator through the pi coding agent for live visibility
jobs.why:
The hand-rolled SemanticAgent loop is correct but opaque: the operator only
sees a final receipt, never the investigator's text, thinking, or tool calls.
That opacity is the practical blocker to trusting the loop at face value and
to iterating on it.

Driving the evaluator through the pi coding agent (the same binary the
openClaw heartbeat runs on) gives live, streaming visibility into the
semantic investigation while preserving every GDDP contract: the typed
submit_verdict terminal tool, the 12-row decision_engine (the trust anchor),
the receipt, and the read-only-where-it-matters invariant. pi is agent-
agnostic and already backs a Microsoft/OpenAI-backed dispatch engine, so it
is not a throwaway choice.

This node lands the harness wiring. The enforcement layer (broad inputs,
enforced outputs) is a sibling node: pi-evaluator-guard. The intent/integrity
verdict contract upgrade is a downstream node: evaluator-intent-integrity-verdict.

jobs.goal: Produce a reviewable result for node canary-retry-proof
jobs.title: Canary: echo utility with documentation requirement
jobs.why:
Proof-of-concept node to exercise the retry loop. The implementation criterion
is designed so the executor will miss it on first attempt, producing a
fail-with-evidence verdict that triggers re-dispatch.

The goal and required_artifacts mention scripts/echo.py, decision.md,
result-summary.md, and patch.diff, but criterion 3 also requires
docs/echo-usage.md. Because that file is neither in the goal nor in
required_artifacts, the executor (Jules) will likely implement the echo
utility and produce the required artifacts without creating the docs file.
The evaluator's semantic lane should then judge criterion 3 as judged_fail
with evidence referencing "docs/echo-usage.md" (a file path), causing
has_criteria_evidence to return True and the retry loop to fire.

jobs.why:

jobs.goal: Produce a reviewable result for node job-state-consistency
jobs.title: Make jobs.status and jobs.queue_state agree on every write path
jobs.why:
baseline.sh reported "running=2" when only one job was truly running: the
failed canary attempt job_20260711T16542651 sits at status=failed,
queue_state=running. At least one live write path updates status without
queue_state (decision_loop/engine.py expiry sets status='expired' only), and
the origin of the inconsistent row is undiagnosed. Every operator-facing
count reads one column or the other, so any divergence makes the dashboard
lie. Small surface, real correctness stakes.
